recipes.name: Quick and Easy American Chop Suey

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook macaroni according to package directions until tender; drain.
Meanwhile, cook and stir ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat until beef is browned and crumbly, about 10 minutes. Drain well. Stir in tomato soup until combined.
Return drained macaroni to the pot. Add beef mixture and stir until well combined. Season with salt and ground black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick and Easy American Chop Suey
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy American chop suey combines elbow macaroni and ground beef in a simple tomato sauce for a family-friendly dinner ready in 25 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I think the younger generation... just doesn't "GET IT!" This is a mid-century recipe from a simpler time, that sooooo many seniors grew up eating (and loved as kids, I might add). It is what it is! You want to add greem pepper, mushrooms, a sprinkle of cheese; I can understand that. BUT... when people completely change the recipe by using marinara sauce, tomato sauce, stewed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, Italian or Mexican spices; it's just NOT the same recipe! And aren't we all getting a bit tired of the BUZZ word "BLAND", it's so freely used to describe so many recipes on this site. PLEASE... like it or not; rate the recipe as written.

Yes and enjoyed it. Added fresh basil, garlic powder, a tsp or so of taco seasoning, one or 2 shakes of chili powder, 1/4 to 1/2 cup parmesan cheese, about 1 tsp white or brown sugar, S and P to taste, and 1/2 cup of water...all to deepen the flavors just a bit. I haven't made made American chop suey often because it never ended up with the flavor I wanted. It was more like marinara. The tomato soup base made all the difference in this comfort food. I simmered the sauce for about 20 minutes before adding the cooked macaroni, then for an additional 5 minutes. Terrific easy recipe for which I thank you. ~Judi David

I have made a similar recipe for years and years. Great for busy nights...especially after work with kids clamouring for dinner. I go a step further by cooking the pasta with the sauce. Add a tsp. of beef bouillon base, or granules or 1 cube to compensate for the extra water you will use. Cook as she says but add about 1 1/2 cups water to it; bring to boil; add the elbows (or other smaller pasta); stir and bring back to boil. Reduce heat to simmer; cover and cook for about 20 min. stirring a few more times.
If you want you can use spaghetti sauce but it isn't meant to taste Italian. I noticed that a few women compared it to goulash and it is that too. You could add some beans and BBQ sauce to it for another variation. Fast, easy, versatile, and rib-sticking!

I made this in my ninja slow cooker, I used 2lbs of meat, 1 diced onion, 1 diced green pepper, 1 TBSP of olive oil, cooked all together on medium on the stove top setting. I left most of the grease in, and added 4 cans of Campbell's tomato soup. I filled half of one of the cans with water and swished it around. Just to thin it a small bit. I added 1 TBSP of basil, oregano, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper to taste. A dash or two of cheyenne pepper. I moved the setting to low on slow cooker. I cooked 1lb of pasta and stirred the sauce occasionally. Added the pasta to the ninja. And serve. My family LOVED it. Normally, I leave recipes alone but I wanted to make it perfect for my family since they are asc buffs. Still a perfect base, I couldn't have done it without it. Thank you!

I've been making this for years with variations I start with 1/4 lb chopped bacon sautée chopped green pepper (1) and chopped onion (1) and minced garlic in the bacon fat. Brown the Hamburg in mixture instead of soup, 28 oz can of crushed tomatoes and 1/2 of 6 oz can of tomato paste and oregano. Mix with 1/2 lb cooked elbow macaroni let sit for 20 mins

My mother made this for many years. It's supposed to have an oriental theme. She used I lb of hamburger, 2 cans of Franco-American spaghetti (now owned by Campbells, I think), onions, some chopped green pepper, and I can of Bean Sprouts (rinsed) just before serving over crispy chow mein noodles. Season with Soy sauce.
It is our "comfort food".

I made this today for tomorrow's dinner. After letting cool for an hour and a half, I put it into a large Tupperware and put in the fridge. From the spoonful I tasted after putting it in the container, I was really pleased with the taste. I added dice onions, celery, green peppers, and canned sliced mushrooms, along with thyme, parsley, and oregano.

I can't imagine I would care for the recipe as written as tomato soup is pretty boring to me (not penalizing the submitter with a low rating, since I obviously didn't follow the recipe.) But this was nearly identical to one of my favorite comfort meals growing up (we called it goulash), but my mom made it different. As an adult, when she told me the ingredients, I was shocked (primarily because I was never a ketchup fan, and as an adult went to a Hungarian restaurant, ordering goulash and realized it's NOTHING like goulash, haha!!!). Mom used ketchup as the base (I know, sounded gross to me too) but once cooked it added a slight sweetness to it. She also added sharp cheddar throughout and sprinkled on top, and added some fresh garlic to the onions after caramelizing. The sweetness of the grilled onions and the sweet/tangy from the ketchup are a great match (and you would never know it was ketchup). I feel odd making it as an adult, but when I want a little comfort and an easy/cheap meal, it's my go-to.

My mom got me into making it this way since I was a kid. She always thought regular tomato sauce was too acidic for her and my great Grammy made it this way also. We only used Campbell's soup because other brands just didn't taste right and it was delicious and it makes it creamier. We do add green peppers, mushrooms , celery, onions, garlic and other seasonings like onion and garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper in with the beef mixture. Once we plate it we put a dash or 2 of celery salt to our liking and its perfect!

Been making this through 3 generations in our family. It's an old standby. We have never used the soup variation, but instead, a large can of crushed tomatoes --home-canned tomatoes being the best. 
 Additions have also included mushrooms, hot pepper flakes and tomato sauce. Also, I reverse the above instructions and recommend transferring the hamburger mix to the drained elbow mac pot due to the volume.

I use tomato sauce or marinara sauce for more flavor. 
Also, start by sauteing bacon first and then cooking onion in the bacon fat. Remove from pan and brown and season chopped beef. Combine all ingredients and you have a very tasty dish!
I ate this as a child when things were much simpler.
OMG! I grew up on this recipe. Everytime I make this for friends they are amazed how good it is and that I use tomato soup and not canned tomatoes.
Grew up with this! The only things I change for dietary needs are ground turkey and no salt tomato sauce. Still my comfort food.
I change the tomato soup to marinara sauce. I put garlic two.

My grandmother grew up in a big family during the depression and then had to manage money during WWII. This meal was a major staple for that generation. It's intended to be tasty enough on its own if it's all you have. Believe me they were grateful for it. It is meant to be like the old Rock Soup Story of old.. just add in whatever you like. My grandmother made it a full meal by making it exactly this way and adding canned peas and sometimes diced canned tomatoes but never another thing. I think if you add too many ingredients you end up with a flavor that does not taste like this. This isn't a recipe, its a flavor. To this day its a comfort food for my brother and I. As the flavor brings back days of old, the smell almost transports you and then you can almost see Nanny with her wooden spoon shaking at us to stop playing at the table and eat our dinner. Thank you for reminding me of this recipe I've been needing to switch things up again! It's just in time for my brother's birthday and I know his wife doesn't make it so it will be a nice surprise! :)
Did not need any more salt- Added Parmeson cheese at the table
Definitely not by any means bad-tasting, but somewhat boring/bland. I think I would add some veggies or spices if I decided to make this again.
